Dentures and bridges

The crown

It covers and protects a badly damaged or root-treated tooth. It can also be fitted on an implant.

Inlays and onlays

A custom-made ceramic or composite piece bonded to the tooth to rebuild the missing part of a damaged tooth. Only the affected area is removed, so it preserves more of the tooth than a crown.

The bridge

It replaces one or two missing teeth by resting on the neighbouring teeth (the abutments), which must be prepared. It is fixed.

Removable dentures

Partial or complete, it replaces several teeth and is taken out for cleaning. A partial denture on a metal framework (cobalt-chrome) rests on the remaining teeth with rests and clasps: it is thin, strong and stable. A denture can also be stabilised with implants.

Complete dentures

When no teeth remain, a complete denture is made entirely of acrylic. In the upper jaw it covers the palate and is held by suction; in the lower jaw it rests on the ridge and leaves room for the tongue, which often makes it less stable. Two implants can then stabilise it.

Implant-retained complete dentures

Implants can stabilise a complete denture: it clips onto attachments fitted to the implants. It no longer moves while chewing and can still be removed for cleaning. In the lower jaw, two implants are often enough; in the upper jaw, four are generally used.

Sources: HAS, inlay and onlay restorations

Further information

The crown

It is a dental prosthesis that protects a tooth, whether alive or not (root-filled). A crown artificially rebuilds the crown of a badly damaged tooth. It can be used alone, or with a post and core (a false stump anchored in the root by a post, which holds the crown in place). The two main advantages: the tooth is protected, and a well-made crown is not noticeable.

The bridge

A bridge replaces a missing tooth, or even two or more in some cases, by resting on the neighbouring teeth, one on each side. The principle is the same as for a crown. The advantage is obvious: it is a fixed system that you do not take out every day to clean. However, the teeth used as abutments must be “crowned”.

Complete dentures

For people with no teeth at all, a complete denture is a solution. It can be stabilised with dental implants.
